description: Banana leaf anthracnose is a fungal disease caused mainly by Colletotrichum musae. It infects banana leaves and other aerial parts of the plant, producing necrotic lesions that may reduce photosynthesis and weaken plant growth. The pathogen can infect plants in the field and remain latent until environmental conditions become favorable for symptom development.
symptoms: Small dark brown to black spots on leaves
Irregular necrotic lesions with defined margins
Yellow halo around lesions in some cases
Expansion of lesions leading to leaf blight
disease_cycle: The fungus survives in infected plant debris or soil.
Spores (conidia) are produced in structures called acervuli on infected tissues.
Conidia spread through rain splash, wind, insects, or contaminated tools.
Spores germinate on leaf surfaces under humid conditions.
The pathogen penetrates tissues using an appressorium and colonizes plant cells.
favorable_conditions: Dense canopy with poor air circulation

cultural_control: Remove and destroy infected leaves and plant debris
biological_control: Use of antagonistic fungi such as Trichoderma spp.
Application of beneficial microbial biocontrol agents
chemical_control: Fungicides such as carbendazim, mancozeb or thiophanate-methyl
Apply according to recommended agricultural guidelines

economic_impact: Anthracnose can reduce plant vigor and contribute to yield losses and fruit quality reduction in banana plantations.

International Journal of Environment and Climate Change – Symptomatology of Colletotrichum musae
